recipes.name: Traditional Sauerbraten
ingredients_raw: 1 cup red wine vinegar, or to taste
10 whole cloves, or more to taste
2 bay leaves, or more to taste
salt and ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Place beef rump roast, onions, vinegar, water, 1 tablespoon salt, 1 tablespoon black pepper, sugar, cloves, and bay leaves in a large pot. Cover and refrigerate for 2 to 3 days, turning meat daily. Remove meat from marinade and pat dry with paper towels, reserving marinade.
Season flour to taste with salt and black pepper in a large bowl. Sprinkle flour mixture over beef.
Heat vegetable oil in a large Dutch oven or pot over medium heat; cook beef until brown on all sides, about 10 minutes.
Pour reserved marinade over beef, cover, and reduce heat to medium-low. Simmer until beef is tender, 3 1/2 to 4 hours.
Remove beef to a platter and slice.
Strain solids from remaining liquid and continue cooking over medium heat. Add gingersnap cookies and simmer until gravy is thickened, about 10 minutes. Serve gravy over sliced beef.

raw_recipe.headline: Traditional Sauerbraten
raw_recipe.description: This sauerbraten is marinated for at least two days for a deeply flavorful roast both tangy and savory. It's easy to see why this is such a classic.

review.reviewBody: I cooked this in the crock pot all day (8 hours - 6 lbs) after marinating it for 5 days. WOW! Excellent falvor! I have made this in the past and it turned out tough - the crockpot is the way to go! Made the gravy with Nabisco Ginger Snaps - A real hit at our German themed dinner party. I also served spatsel, red cabbage, mashed potatoes and sourdough rolls with Lingonberry jam. Excellent!

My grandmother’s recipe (born in 1903), was passed down from her grandmother (Germany 1860’s), used more ginger snaps which was dissolved in the original liquid used as marinade. This prevents any lumps. She served it with knedliky, a Czechoslovakian dumpling. Also, she marinated carrots and celery along with the onions in the pot with the meat and cooked the carrots and onions in the Dutch oven in the oven at 325 for at LEAST 5-7 hours WITH THE marinade after browning the meat. This makes for a moister meat. Otherwise, the recipe looks correct. (I’m 100% German but 3rd generation American).

It was good. I have also used a recipe that marinated for three days, using cider vinegar instead of red wine vinegar, and involved rubbing the meat with a mixture of dry ground ginger and salt before putting in the marinade. One trick I learned is to brown it well on all sides, then place in a Dutch oven, pour over the marinade with spices and onions, and bake covered four hours at 300 degrees F. When done, strain the cooking liquid and save it, then chill it and the meat overnight. Slice the next day, place in a shallow pan, pour over beef broth and warm covered in a slow oven for one hour. Make the gravy with the strained and defatted cooking liquid, adding finely crushed gingersnaps by the handful and whisking them in until blended before adding more. The recipe came from a German lady who ran a deli, but the rewarming in broth step is mine. It makes the meat melt in your mouth.

I made this for my wife who's father was German and loved sauerbraten. The marinade was spot on and was perfect. We marinated the 3.5 lb chuck roast for 2 days in a plastic bag, flipping 2x a day. I put it in a slow cooker on high with the marinade for 6 hours and the 1 hour on medium. I made the gravy in a pot, after straining the solids and I substituted 2 tbs ginger paste and 1/2C sugar for the gingersnaps and boiled it down for about 20 min. Everyone loved it and we served it with red cabbage and spatezel. Fantastic!

Holy this freaking amazing! Seriously I have no words for how amazing this was. Thank you so much! I studied abroad in Germany I find this to be comfort food. Since we are finally getting some cold and snow I thought it was time for a nice hearty meal. This was quite easy to make. I marinated it in my crock pot as I don't have a dutch oven big enough. I did add some extra red wine vinegar to the marinade because I love it. Then I browned it in skillet and put it back in my crock pot for about 7 hours. Don't forget to let it rest before you slice it. It was very tender and just made my tongue explode with flavor.
Hi, this is not a german Sauerbraten. I`m german, live in Cologne and over here we cook ist different. No Ginger in a traditional Sauerbraten.

OUTSTANDING!!! I bought made 2 roasts in seperate ziplock bags and marinated for 2 days then double bagged and put in the freezer. Took one to my daughters 4 hours away and finished thawing in the fridge at her home. (the meat continued marinating as it thawed). I used at slow cooker on this roast, 8 hours on low. I transferred the juices to a sauce pan (through a strainer) added the ginger snaps. It was so good.

The second roast was cooked on the stove. simmered for 4 hours. I think it was even better. My daughter said it tasted the same.

Used the german spaetzel recipe. WINNER WINNER GERMAN DINNER!!

Thank you for sharing your grandmother's recipe. My grandmother was born in Germany and she made this on special occasions. It was a family favorite! I wish I had her recipe. Every time I crave sauerbraten I'd have to go to my favorite German restaurant. No more! Your recipe came out perfect! The only changes I made were adding a little pickling spice and some red wine (I used 5 lbs of meat). I also cooked it in a slow cooker on low for 8-9 hours. It came out just like my grandmother's sauerbraten - tender and tasty! Brought me back to my childhood. Danke schön!! :)

Very, very good! We followed the recipe as it was written. The only exception was adding a bit of beef broth during the simmering of the meat, and then, after slicing up the meat and dissolving the ginger snaps in the gravy, we added the meat slices to it as well. Let that go for about 10-15 minutes and all came out quite tasty. Had it for Christmas dinner and everyone raved about how good it was. Will definitely make this again. Oh, yes, have to add that finding juniper berries was challenging.

This is a simple recipe and it turned out great. I went a little stronger with more vinegar less water and added more cloves. I also marinated for 6 days. The longer marination I think is key. I also cut the meat into 4 sections instead of leaving it whole. That helps get the flavor all the way into the meat. Great recipe, I’ll be using this again.

This is exactly like my great-grandmother's recipe. The only difference is that we use chuck roast and cut the meat into 2" cubes. This way it only needs to marinate overnight. I also make my own gingersnaps because I can't fine any store bought that taste good. This is an absolute family favorite!
okay

I make this in my pressure cooker and it comes out wonderful every time. My family will totally leave no left overs and I have to make sure that I have cooked extra egg noodles for the gravy. I always add a few extra gingersnaps to the gravy for a nice zing.

My Grandparents on my Moms side are both German The Differences are Subtle but noticeable We use a Whole Brisket with the Point Portion still attached Use a really Cheap white vinegar, the good stuff is too strong according to Grandma, Drinkable red wine, and Pickling Spices and plain water doubling the amounts of wine and vinegar

Loved it!! I substituted the beef roast for pork tenderloin and didn’t add the ginger snap cookies (weird) and used about half the vinegar called for, and adjusted some of the spices and seasonings and added cayenne for that spicy kick!! Turned out wonderful!!!

I used this marinade, but sliced meat and let sit for about 6-7 hrs, turning ever hr. Then removed meat, floured, fried to brown, added marinade and simmered on low for 1 1/2 hrs. I did add more vinegar and water, equal parts, and 1 teaspoon of powdered ginger, as I did t have ginger snaps. ..it was excellent! Next time I’ll get ginger snaps!
The recipe was easy enough. My husband rated it above his highest recipe-rating numbers!! He’s never done that before!

This was the first time I made sauerbraten. I had it at a German restaurant and once that restaurant closed I never had it again. I made it exactly according to the recipe. It came out fantastic. Everyone loved it. My dad never had it in his life and he really enjoyed it. He said he never had anything like it. It all went the next day for leftovers. I will definitely make this exact recipe again. I actually can't wait. Thank you!!!!

It was a nice throw back to my childhood. I might make it next time with wine instead of vinegar or half of each. The gingersnaps in the gravy were a nice touch. I made it with Kartoffelklöße (German Potato Dumplings) and warm red cabbage and it was great!!

There are a few changes I would make to this recipe.... I always use a good red wine, I add Juniper berries and I marinate it for a minimum of 5 days. My grandmother was born in New Biedeck, Russia and made great German food. I inherited my love of German food from her.
